name: Javan Oriole
rangeDescription: Java
description: Rare oriole endemic to the mossy montane forests of Java. Male is glossy black with a crimson breast and wing spot, while the female is dull black overall with a dirty-pink breast and belly; note pale bill on both.

name: Cameroon Mountain Greenbul
rangeDescription: Montane forest of nigeria and cameroon
description: A medium-sized greenbul of the mountains of Cameroon and southeastern Nigeria. Remarkably uniform yellow-olive in plumage, with a red eye.

name: Watercock
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern and eastern asia and malay archipelago
description: Large, distinctive marsh dweller, elusive and often difficult to see in the heavily vegetated wet fields and marshes it inhabits. Male is unmistakable, with black body, brown-edged wing coverts, and red-and-yellow bill with raised, spiky red frontal shield (unlike smaller moorhen).

name: Black-backed Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Humid foothills of southeastern peru (cusco and puno)
description: Tiny, boldly-colored flycatcher. Compact and short-tailed; yellow below, black above, with a white throat and mustache, and small red shoulder patch.

name: Short-tailed Paradigalla
rangeDescription: Patchily distributed mountains of western and central new guinea
description: A medium-sized, short-tailed bird of montane forest. All black plumage with iridescence on the head, fairly long bill and a distinctive, yellow wattle between the eye and the bill.

name: Orange-cheeked Honeyeater
rangeDescription: West-central new guinea (timberline zone of snow mountains)
description: A fairly large honeyeater of upper montane and subalpine forest and shrubbery. Overall olive color, light streaking with paler grayish belly and yellow legs.

name: Chestnut Seedeater
rangeDescription: Paraguay to south-central brazil, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Handsome seedeater. Males are mostly chestnut with a gray cap, wings, and tail, while females are sandy-colored and difficult to separate from other female seedeaters.

name: Streak-breasted Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Eastern lesser sundas (timor and semau)
description: A fairly small honeyeater of lowland and foothill wooded areas on Timor. Olive-gray upperparts with greenish wing feathers, pale underparts with thick, dark streaks, sometimes looking like white streaks on a dark background.

name: White-bearded Greenbul
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria and cameroon to gabon, angola, and northern democratic republic of the congo
description: A medium-sized greenbul often found in flocks in forest and forest edge with other bearded-greenbuls. Like all bearded-greenbuls, will sometimes puff out throat feathers.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Gray-green Scrubwren
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of new guinea
description: A small bird of lower montane forest interior. Whitish belly, pale gray head and greenish wing.

name: Banded Kestrel
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands and subdesert of madagascar
description: Atypical kestrel that is marked more like a small hawk, with a gray back and a barred belly. Uncommon to rare Madagascar endemic that is found patchily across the island in and adjacent to forest.

name: Biak Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Numfor and biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A fairly small bird of wooded areas on the Bay Islands. Low crest is flattened at the front and rounded at the back.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Golden-tailed Parrotlet
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (pernambuco to são paulo)
description: Small parrot with a short, squared tail. The body is largely green with distinctive brown bases to the wings and an orangey face.

name: Edwards's Pheasant
rangeDescription: Lowlands of central vietnam (on verge of extinction in wild)
description: Critically endangered species with tiny populations in remote hilly terrain of central Vietnam, where it inhabits densely vegetated hillsides with dense low cover. There are no recent reports of the species in the wild.

name: Orange-throated Sunangel
rangeDescription: Andes of northeastern colombia to northwestern venezuela (southern lara to táchira)
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with a short, straight bill found in the Andes of Venezuela and eastern Colombia. Male has a green body, buff and green spotted underparts, and a glittering orange throat.

name: Superb Parrot
rangeDescription: Interior southeastern australia (new south wales and northern victoria)
description: Large, elegant green parrot with long pointed tail, found in inland New South Wales region. Male has bright yellow face with red throat band.

name: White-spotted Munia
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern new guinea (lorentz river eastward at least to the kikori river region, and perhaps farther eastward)
description: A small brown bird with a heavy blue bill, rufous underparts, and white spotting across the head, back, and breast. The pale buff rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Nicobar Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Nicobar islands
description: A large pigeon with greenish-brown upperparts, gray head, and gray underparts. Occurs in small flocks that feed on fruits and berries in the canopy.

name: Black-throated Prinia
rangeDescription: Eastern nepal to sikkim, bhutan, southeastern tibet, and arunachal pradesh
description: Very long tailed prinia of hilly and montane areas, descending to foothills in winter. Plain with brown upperparts, slightly rustier on the wing, and paler belly.

name: Plumed Egret
rangeDescription: Eastern indonesia, new guinea, and australia
description: A stocky egret that is larger than Eastern Cattle and Little Egrets, but smaller than the Great Egret. Often confusing and difficult to identify, this bird is truly intermediate between potential confusion species.
